title: PROBE: VLM-Guided Discrete Structural Reconfiguration for Customized and Efficient Video Retrieval

problem.claim: Efficient video retrieval methods need to compare the same videos under different semantic criteria rather than a single fixed similarity notion.

gap.claim: Criterion-dependent video comparison remains largely unexplored in efficient hashing-based retrieval frameworks.

contributions.claim: PROBE uses a frozen vision-language model to inject semantic structure into a reusable binary hash index.
Prompts act as discrete operators that select criterion-relevant hash subspaces and enable customized video comparison through masked distance computation.

Criterion-induced subspace regularization transfers prompt-conditioned semantic geometry into hash subspaces while preserving local relational consistency, alongside global alignment and reconstruction for stabilization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that one model trained jointly on heterogeneous video datasets consistently outperforms strong video hashing baselines.
The authors report effective generalization to unseen datasets and diverse retrieval criteria.
The authors report that source code is available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing self-supervised video hashing uses compact binary representations but generally imposes one fixed global similarity geometry.
Real-world retrieval may require criterion-dependent comparisons, a capability largely unexplored in efficient hashing frameworks.

PROBE uses a frozen vision-language model, reusable hash representations, prompts, criterion-conditioned subspaces, masked distances, and regularization objectives to reconfigure similarity structure.
The authors report improved baseline performance and generalization across datasets and retrieval criteria.

source_observation.claim: A single binary representation can be reused while prompts select criterion-relevant semantic subspaces for comparison.

interpretation.claim: Separating reusable storage from query-conditioned comparison may support multiple semantic retrieval objectives without rebuilding the index.

application.claim: Consider prompt- or criterion-conditioned subspace selection when designing efficient retrieval systems serving heterogeneous similarity requirements.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach remains effective when prompts are ambiguous or criteria conflict.

source_observation.claim: The method combines criterion-conditioned regularization with global alignment and reconstruction.

interpretation.claim: Maintaining global structure alongside specialized subspaces may reduce instability across views and datasets.

application.claim: When adapting a shared representation to multiple criteria, pair local criterion-specific objectives with a global stabilization objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the trade-off between criterion specialization and preservation of the full hash space.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baseline identities, quantitative results, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not describe prompt construction, model architecture details, or computational costs.
The abstract does not independently verify the reported performance or code availability.
